about_blocks.text: About Valiant Recovery in Kelowna, British Columbia
about_blocks.html: About Valiant Recovery in Kelowna, British Columbia

about_blocks.text: Valiant Recovery runs a private residential addiction program out of a large family home on Lakeshore Road in Kelowna, in BC's Okanagan Valley. The company calls the Kelowna house its premier location and says it was founded there in 2010. It is the western site of Valiant Recovery Inc., which also runs Valiant Behavioural Health near Ottawa.
about_blocks.html: Valiant Recovery runs a private residential addiction program out of a large family home on Lakeshore Road in Kelowna, in BC's Okanagan Valley. The company calls the Kelowna house its premier location and says it was founded there in 2010. It is the western site of Valiant Recovery Inc., which also runs Valiant Behavioural Health near Ottawa.

about_blocks.text: The program is built around very small numbers. Valiant's website currently advertises a 2-client maximum, and older pages describe up to 5 clients at once, so ask admissions what the current cap is. Either way, clients get a lot of private time with counsellors. The site promises 40 one-to-one sessions a month, plus daily groups on anxiety, depression, grief and loss, anger, codependency, trauma, the 12 steps and relapse prevention.

about_blocks.text: Stays run 30, 60, 90 or 120 days. Clients need to be sober before they move in, and Valiant can arrange detox ahead of treatment for people entering its residential program. Spiritual counselling and Christian content are part of the program, and recovery.com notes that clients are not pressured to take part and can choose other therapies. Other courses include the Genesis Process for relapse prevention, EMDR for trauma, art therapy, and stress and healthy lifestyle sessions.

about_blocks.text: The house is about 4,700 square feet, with 6 bedrooms and 7 bathrooms. A self-contained 2 bedroom suite with its own entrance lets women sleep separately from men. There is a great room with a two-storey marble fireplace where most groups happen, a home theatre with a 150 inch screen, a gym, a hot tub, an infrared sauna and a backyard patio where meals and art therapy move outside in summer.

about_blocks.text: Valiant is a pay-for-fee centre and is not covered by provincial health care. Recovery.com lists an estimated $10,500 to $32,000 CDN per month, and Medicard financing is available. Aftercare phone or video counselling is included for every month you stay, and the centre offers a free month of treatment to 90 day graduates who relapse after completing their aftercare plan.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Valiant Recovery Kelowna

faqs.question: What kind of program is Valiant Recovery Kelowna?

answer_blocks.text: It is a private residential (inpatient) addiction program run in a large house in Kelowna, British Columbia. Clients live on site for 30, 60, 90 or 120 days. Valiant says it takes a maximum of 2 clients at a time, so most of the work happens in one-to-one counselling rather than big groups.
answer_blocks.html: It is a private residential (inpatient) addiction program run in a large house in Kelowna, British Columbia. Clients live on site for 30, 60, 90 or 120 days. Valiant says it takes a maximum of 2 clients at a time, so most of the work happens in one-to-one counselling rather than big groups.

faqs.question: How much does Valiant Recovery Kelowna cost?

answer_blocks.text: Recovery.com lists an estimated $10,500 to $32,000 CDN per month. Valiant does not post prices on its own site and says the fee depends on the program level, the length of stay and whether detox is needed, so call admissions for an information package with pricing.
answer_blocks.html: Recovery.com lists an estimated $10,500 to $32,000 CDN per month. Valiant does not post prices on its own site and says the fee depends on the program level, the length of stay and whether detox is needed, so call admissions for an information package with pricing.

faqs.question: Is Valiant Recovery covered by BC public health care?

answer_blocks.text: No. Valiant Recovery Inc. is a pay-for-fee service and says it is not government funded or covered by provincial health care. It accepts cheques, cash, debit, major credit cards and wire transfers, offers Medicard financing, and notes that some private insurers may pay part of the cost.

faqs.question: Does Valiant Recovery Kelowna offer detox?

answer_blocks.text: Clients must be clean and sober before they move into the house. Valiant says it can arrange detox before treatment when it is needed, but only for people going on to its residential program. Its FAQ adds that anyone who arrives still in withdrawal is taken to a hospital or local detox centre at their own expense.

answer_blocks.text: Valiant's site advertises 40 private one-to-one sessions a month, around 10 a week, on top of daily group sessions. Groups cover topics such as anxiety and depression, grief and loss, anger, codependency, trauma, the 12 steps and relapse prevention.

faqs.question: Where is Valiant Recovery Kelowna and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: The house is on Lakeshore Road in Kelowna's Lower Mission area, near the Okanagan Lake beaches. From Vancouver it is about 4 hours by car over the Coquihalla and Highway 97C, or about an hour's flight into Kelowna International Airport. Kamloops is roughly 2 hours away and Vernon and Penticton about an hour.

faqs.question: Can family visit or stay in touch?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Approved family members can visit on weekends and Valiant offers family therapy sessions during the visit at no extra charge. Visitors stay in nearby hotels. Phone calls and emails are allowed at set times and may be monitored.

faqs.question: What support is there after I leave?

answer_blocks.text: Valiant includes 5 hours of phone or video counselling for every 30 days of treatment, or 10 hours on the Executive Program. Before discharge a follow-up counsellor helps you set up support groups at home, and Soberlink breathalyzer monitoring is available for people recovering from alcohol use.
